findings.title: The Hand as a Bounded Channel
findings.claim: In the surrounding commands, the hand that cannot reach an owed recipient and the hand extended without measure become two failures of circulation: one withholds material provision, the other exhausts the giver. The bound hand and the overextended hand remain bodily images while the pericope makes their economic consequence legible.
findings.mechanism: 17:26 directs provision to named rights-holders and rejects waste; 17:27 names spendthrifts. Those independent acts meet the focus limb, its binding, its extension, and its seated depletion. The contact turns opposite hand postures into a shared question of whether provision can move to its proper recipient while capacity remains usable.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees both the claimant who needs the hand to move and the giver who must retain capacity; moderation is not merely a midpoint between two labels.
findings.containment: This does not prescribe a numerical budget or make every gift wasteful. The literal bound and extended hand stays recoverable, and the context supports a circulation reading without making the two failures identical.

epistemic.reason: The channel supports and focus branch records are trusted and lexically registered; the integrated macro consequence is still an interpretation of their contact with 17:26-27.

findings.title: Material Limit, Open Relation
findings.claim: The pericope distinguishes a hand that cannot give at a moment from a person who has closed the relationship: 17:28 permits a material turning-away under constraint but still requires accessible speech, while 17:23-24 make beneficence, protective humility, and mercy active forms of care.
findings.mechanism: The focus binding supplies a material limit. The surrounding care commands and the explicit speech alternative in 17:28 independently meet that limit, so the focus's closed hand need not entail withdrawn mercy or acknowledgment. The focus verb's registered social-openness branch adds a bounded echo when the nearby verse keeps speech open.
findings.reader_payoff: An empty or restrained hand need not make a person absent to the claimant; the reader can distinguish inability to transfer from refusal of all relation.
findings.containment: This does not claim that 17:28 is the same event as 17:29 or that gracious speech substitutes for a due transfer. The relational reading is an attributed contextual inference, with the material hand image intact.

epistemic.reason: All cited HFT context coordinates and roots match the supplied context projection, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound; the reading is retained as attributed context rather than independent lexical proof.

findings.title: The Closing Frame of Agency
findings.claim: 17:39 repeats the focus's prohibition to make a state and its blamed consequence, but places that frame beside the warning against assigning another deity. The echo can let the hand command speak about bounded creaturely agency as well as private resource technique, without equating the acts.
findings.mechanism: The focus's make-state verb and passive blame meet the same verb and blame in the closing command; the separate object of ultimate allegiance supplies the frame's limit. The registered naming branch of the repeated verb can also color the closing use as an act of assigning status.
findings.reader_payoff: The hand is neither an absolute gatekeeper nor an inexhaustible source; its real capacity sits within a passage that marks ultimate allegiance as a boundary.
findings.containment: The two prohibitions and their offenses are not equivalent. The connection may be a rhetorical frame without semantic transfer; the agency reading remains an exploratory, attributed extension and does not displace the resource reading.

epistemic.reason: Exact repeated surface forms support the contact, while the inference from structural echo to bounded agency is expressly tentative and retains its alternative.

findings.title: Total Extension and Fatigue
findings.claim: The focus's كُلَّ البسط grammatically remains total extension, yet its ending in depletion can carry a qualified root-image echo of fatigue. The later 'all' over accountable faculties and gathered acts puts that single exhaustive release beside a continuing field of responsibility.
findings.mechanism: The focus totalizer carries the registered whole/all branch, while the same focus root also has a distinct blunting-and-fatigue branch and the final word names depletion. The independent later totalizers at 17:36 and 17:38 frame faculties and acts that continue to be answerable; together these contacts let one exhaustive act image consuming the capacity needed for the rest.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive total outflow as a cost to the actor's continuing capacity, not only a maximum quantity.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory root-image echo. كُلَّ means totality here, not fatigue; the fatigue branch never replaces 'all,' and the continuing-obligations contrast is attributed rather than grammatically forced.

epistemic.reason: The focus and context coordinates match, and the packet itself bounds this as a surprising root echo; the multi-step contact remains inferential.

findings.mechanism: The registered long-distance/full-reach branch on the focus extension meets 17:37's failed penetration, failed attainment, and limit of length. That distinct bodily scene returns through the focus hand and its depleted ending, changing total extension from spending alone into an image of finite personal reach.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why total extension can fail as an assertion of boundless agency even beyond the immediate resource scene.
findings.containment: The verses concern different actions: 17:37 addresses walking in pride and bodily reach, not expenditure. This is an attributed analogy, not a substitute for the hand's primary material image.

epistemic.reason: The context roots and coordinates match the packet, and the independent connection nomination notes the domain difference; the finite-reach transfer remains analogical.

findings.title: Depletion as Regret for Loss
findings.claim: With 17:27 immediately warning against waste, the focus's final depleted state can also carry grief for what has been lost beyond recovery. The ending is then not only an exhausted capacity but a possible regret over squandered provision.
findings.mechanism: The focus word's supplied analysis includes regretful pressure, and its mapped root registry contains a distinct branch for regret over something missed or lost. The spendthrift named in 17:27 independently supplies the lost-resource trigger; together they make the emotional consequence newly legible.
findings.reader_payoff: The consequence of waste can be felt as the grief of irretrievable loss, not only the arithmetic fact of having spent too much.
findings.containment: The focus's depletion and exposure remain the ordinary reading. The regret branch is a context-activated possibility, not an assertion that remorse is explicit or inevitable.

epistemic.reason: The focus analysis and accepted root branch provide the regret reading, while trusted channel evidence and the explicit anti-waste connection supply the context; the resulting emotional link remains interpretive.

findings.containment: The focus phrase still describes a hand bound to its owner's neck. The pledge use is a contextual echo from a distinct attested expression, not a claim that this verse literally makes a covenant or invokes a legal pledge.

epistemic.reason: The lexical branch and exact covenant trigger are supplied, but their contact is an analogical contextual inference and the contextual support carries legacy_unbound provenance.

findings.title: Capacity Within Sought Aid
findings.claim: As a Phase 2 overlay, Fātiḥa 1:5's 'we seek help' can tint the focus hand's capacity as dependent rather than self-sufficient: the hand is neither made inert nor treated as the sole source of what it can give.
findings.mechanism: The focus hand has an available, registered capacity branch; the individual external occurrence at 1:5:4 explicitly asks for aid. That separate act meets the focus carrier and changes the bounded hand from a self-contained resource into capacity exercised while seeking help.
findings.reader_payoff: The two prohibited extremes become legible as failures of dependent agency: restraint need not mean paralysis, and action need not pretend to inexhaustible self-sufficiency.
findings.containment: This overlay adds no amount, recipient, or budget rule, and it does not displace the native provision and accountability readings. It is an exploratory contact through one explicitly supplied ayah, not an imported whole-Fātiḥa theme.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies exact surface occurrences for both carrier and trigger, but no source trust label for this cross-surah overlay; the semantic transfer remains an explicitly bounded inference.
